dashboard-views.title: One dashboard, several views
points: Keep views side by side: operations, costs, quality, or one per project
Each view can be filtered to a project and a time range
New views are made while editing the dashboard: empty, as a copy, or from a template

workflows-start.title: Three places to start from
points: Blueprints are empty frames that show how blocks connect: run one, look at it, replace the placeholders
Templates are finished flows for one purpose; the pool offers ready-made workflows from a local folder
Each is only a starting point: every step can be changed, and a blank workflow works too

run-steps.title: Every step says what it was
points: Deterministic steps give the same result for the same input, AI steps can vary, human steps wait for a decision
Follow the run live, then read back every step with its output
The definition hash shows exactly which version of the workflow ran

run-failed.title: A failed run keeps what it did
points: The step that failed is marked, with its output and the reason
The steps before it keep their results, so you can see how far it got
Turn the failure into a TODO so it isn't lost; next time a retry block or a plan B can catch a shaky step

approval-waiting.title: The run is waiting for you
points: Nothing is stuck: the workflow stops at this step on purpose
After your answer it continues from here, not from the top
You can close this dialog and answer later, until the step's time limit runs out (30 minutes unless the step sets another)

todos-sources.title: Where TODOs come from
points: Write them down yourself, or let a workflow create them: with a block or from its gate result
A failed run becomes a TODO with one click
Coding agents add them through the API, so side findings don't evaporate

projects-directory.title: A project is a directory
points: Every workflow belongs to exactly one project, and its steps work with that project's files
AI calls run on this machine; a container for the project is optional
Archiving can be undone: the project and its workflows are kept

project-context.title: What every run knows about this project
points: The AI context is a text that every AI step of a run in this project receives, with every provider
It can be generated from a scan of the directory and then edited by hand
Below are all workflows of the project with their blocks and runs

workflow-versions.title: Every change becomes a version
points: Changes to the flow (blocks, instructions, model, provider) create a new version; name and description don't
Restoring an old version adds it as the newest one; later versions stay in the history
Provider and model apply to the whole workflow; a single AI block can override them for itself

runs-list.title: All runs in one place
points: The runs of every workflow, newest first; your filters are remembered
A run can be repeated: with the workflow's current version and the inputs it had back then
Finished runs are deleted after 90 days by default; the period can be changed

approvals-inbox.title: Everything that is waiting for you
points: Runs waiting for an approval or an input, across all workflows, oldest first
Each question has a time limit; when it runs out, the step fails or takes its default value
Waiting questions don't survive a restart of the instance: the run then counts as interrupted

schedules-timing.title: Workflows at set times
points: Recurring by cron (six fields, seconds first), once at a point in time, or after a delay
Times that fall into standby or a restart are caught up once or skipped, depending on the setting
While the workflow is still running, the next time starts no second run next to it by default

calendar-overview.title: What was planned and what ran
points: The next time of every active schedule and the past runs of all workflows
Red means failed; the calendar only shows, schedules are changed on the schedule itself

cockpit-overview.title: TODOs across all projects
points: At the top is what needs you: TODOs you wrote down, critical ones and overdue ones, from every project
One card per project, split into yours and those from machines: workflows and agents
Automatic TODOs nobody has touched for a long time can be archived in one go

activity-events.title: What happened on this instance
points: Platform events: runs finished or failed, schedules fired or skipped, rejected sign-ins
The output of single steps is in the run itself, not here
Entries expire on their own: information after 7 days, warnings and errors after 30

dlq-retry.title: Failed runs to follow up
points: Runs that end on a failed step land here; cancelled and interrupted ones don't
Retry starts the workflow's current version from the top, with the inputs from back then
Discard only marks the entry as handled; the run is kept

wishes-loop.title: Describe a goal, get workflows
points: A wish is free text for a project: the AI breaks it down into new workflows, and several of them into a chain
It runs them, judges the result and improves it, for up to five rounds
Without automatic improvement you approve twice: the breakdown and the result

factory-create.title: Workflows from a description
points: Describe what a workflow should do, and the AI builds it in the chosen project
A repair rewrites the definition as a new version, so every fix stays traceable
Automatic repair of failing workflows stays off until it is switched on in the settings or for a workflow

chains-sequence.title: Finished workflows, one after another
points: A chain runs its workflows strictly in order, never in parallel, and may mix projects
Each workflow receives the result of the previous one's last step as {{ previous_chain_output }}
Whether a failure stops the chain is set for the chain and for each of its steps

skills-packages.title: Skills: packaged know-how
points: A skill bundles capabilities with an AI context of its own; a workflow activates it and uses it through a skill-capability block
Capabilities that write stay blocked unless the block explicitly allows writing
Built-in skills can't be deleted

webhooks-trigger.title: Start a workflow from outside
points: Each webhook starts one workflow; the token in its URL is the only credential, so treat the URL like a password
Fields of the JSON body become variables of the run and are treated as untrusted input
At most 10 calls per minute from one address; a disabled webhook rejects every call

integrations-connect.title: Connect external services
points: Workflows use connections through the integration block; TODOs can also be exported to GitHub, Jira or Trello
Some services sign in via OAuth with an app you register yourself, others with a token or without credentials
Credentials are stored encrypted; testing a connection runs a real action against the service

debug-failing.title: Workflows whose last run went wrong
points: Every workflow whose latest run failed or finished with errors; it drops off after its next successful run
A restart runs the workflow's current version from the first step, with the original inputs

audit-findings.title: Findings with a memory
points: Findings come from audit workflows: one that isn't seen again is resolved, one that comes back reopens as a regression
An accepted risk keeps a snapshot of its evidence; if the measured value gets noticeably worse, it opens again
Critical and high findings with verified evidence get a TODO automatically

insights-numbers.title: How your runs are doing
points: Duration, cost, tokens, block types and failure reasons of your runs, also per model and provider
Project and time filters apply to durations, costs and trends; success rate and totals always count all runs
Costs are partly estimates, depending on what the provider reports

onboarding-profiles.title: Instructions for coding agents
points: MySuricates writes these texts into projects, as .claude/rules/mysuricates.md or AGENTS.md, so agents such as Claude Code or Codex can talk to the instance
The base always comes along; which profiles are added and in which language is set per project
The instance fills in its own address and how to read the API key; a foreign AGENTS.md is never overwritten

simple-home.title: Simple is for using
points: This is where you start workflows, answer their questions and read what came out of them
Building and configuring belong in Pro: that is where all the steps, options and tools live that would only get in the way while you just use things
Whatever leads to Pro is marked, so you never switch surfaces without noticing

simple-result.title: The result first, then the way there
points: The top shows what the run came to: its report, its last output or the reason it failed
How it got there is in the details, step by step, kept closed until you need them

simple-create.title: Templates are ready-made workflows
points: A template already brings all its steps: create it, give it a project and start it, without building anything
The pool holds more finished workflows; some of them only fit one particular project

build-from-description.title: Building from a description is off here
points: The assistant and the workflow factory build a workflow from a description in words; wishes break a goal down into several workflows
All three are optional, still experimental modules and not part of the default preset core, which is why this instance has none of them

To switch them on at startup: ./scripts/setup.sh --preset research --force brings the assistant, --preset full also the factory and wishes; one at a time with automation.modules.assistant: true (likewise factory, wishes). Where the instance allows it, also in the settings

goals-overview.title: Goals across projects
points: A goal collects TODOs from several projects that work towards one outcome, such as a release
Progress counts the finished TODOs; open questions are listed separately because they have to be settled before the work starts
Reached and archived goals are kept, they just move out of sight

goal-relation-map.title: Where TODOs come from and who works on them
points: On the left is the origin: a workflow run, an audit finding, a health check, an agent or a person
Next to it, which workflow works on a TODO: as the fix workflow on the TODO or through a matching TodoTrigger, and what its last run did
A dotted stub shows where no workflow docks on yet; dashed rows are suggestions that might belong to the goal

goal-timeline.title: The goal on a timeline
points: Every row is a milestone, below them the TODOs without a milestone – each on its due day
A milestone is reached once all TODOs assigned to it are done; its diamond shows where it stands: green reached, yellow due soon, red overdue
Whatever has no date yet waits under “Unplanned”; overdue TODOs turn red and also show up under “Needs you” in the cockpit

goal-guard.title: One guard per goal
points: A workflow from the “Goal guard” template checks the goal every day: overdue and soon-due TODOs and milestones, progress and target date
The result appears as a traffic-light tile on the dashboard; the workflow needs no model and costs no tokens
Switching it off only pauses the schedule – workflow and tile stay, and switching it on again carries on from there

dialogs-sessions.title: Turn a Claude Code session into a workflow
points: Reads the Claude Code sessions on this machine, grouped by project
An analysis looks for repeatable steps and suggests blocks; the confidence says how sure it is about the pattern
Check the suggestions before creating the workflow, especially at low confidence

docs-reading.title: This installation's manuals
points: The documentation from the docs folder: building workflows, architecture, API, operations and development
English where a translation exists, otherwise the German version
The assistant draws on parts of it when you ask about building workflows
